B3-MLO-01-1.title: MLflow Tracking documentation
B3-MLO-01-1.supports: Describes tracking as an API and UI for logging parameters, code versions, metrics and output files, and says a run records metadata (metrics, parameters, start and end times) plus artifacts such as model weights.

B3-MLO-01-4.title: PyTorch reproducibility notes
B3-MLO-01-4.supports: States that completely reproducible results are not guaranteed across releases, individual commits or platforms; results may differ between CPU and GPU even with identical seeds; DataLoader workers need worker_init_fn and a generator for reproducibility; cuDNN benchmark mode may select different algorithms on subsequent runs; deterministic-algorithm mode exists and may raise an error for operations with no deterministic implementation.

B3-MLO-01-4.title: NumPy parallel random number generation
B3-MLO-01-4.supports: Documents SeedSequence.spawn / Generator.spawn for creating (with very high probability) independent streams for parallel workers, and warns against deriving worker seeds as root_seed + worker_id.

B3-MLO-01-5.title: MLflow Tracking documentation
B3-MLO-01-5.supports: Describes tracking as an API and UI for logging parameters, code versions, metrics and output files, and says a run records metadata (metrics, parameters, start and end times) plus artifacts such as model weights.

B3-MLO-01-5.title: MLflow Model Registry
B3-MLO-01-5.supports: Registry holds numbered versions of registered models, mutable aliases pointing to versions, and lineage links to the producing run/logged model/notebook (immutability of versions is not stated by this page).

B3-MLO-01-6.title: DVC data versioning
B3-MLO-01-6.supports: Describes a small .dvc metadata file, kept in Git, that records an MD5 hash of the data and acts as a placeholder; data goes to a hash-addressed cache and checking out a Git commit followed by dvc checkout restores the matching data version.

B3-MLO-01-6.title: DVC command reference: gc
B3-MLO-01-6.supports: Garbage collection removes cache objects not referenced within the chosen scope, so retention scope decides whether old datasets survive.

B3-MLO-01-6.title: DVC internal files (cache structure)
B3-MLO-01-6.supports: A directory is stored as a .dir entry mapping its files to their hashes.

B3-MLO-02-1.title: The ML Test Score: A Rubric for ML Production Readiness and Technical Debt Reduction
B3-MLO-02-1.supports: Lists tests including 'Feature expectations are captured in a schema', 'Model quality is sufficient on important data slices', 'A simpler model is not better', 'The impact of model staleness is known', 'Offline and online metrics correlate', 'Training is reproducible', 'The ML pipeline is integration tested', 'Model quality is validated before serving', 'Models are canaried before serving', 'Serving models can be rolled back', 'Data invariants hold for inputs' and 'Training and serving are not skewed'.

B3-MLO-02-1.title: Rules of Machine Learning (Google)
B3-MLO-02-1.supports: Rule 5: test the infrastructure independently from the machine learning (check that feature columns are populated; check the exported model gives the same score as the training-environment model). Rule 8: know the freshness requirements of the system. Rule 9: do sanity checks right before exporting a model. Rule 29: log the features used at serving time.

B3-MLO-02-7.supports: Tasks that can be retried should produce the same outcome on every re-run, and inserting on a re-run can create duplicate rows (use upsert/overwrite).

B3-MLO-03-1.title: MLflow Model Registry
B3-MLO-03-1.supports: Registry is a centralized model store with versioning (each registration increments the version), lineage to the producing run, tags and annotations; aliases are mutable named references to a model version.

B3-MLO-03-2.title: pickle - Python object serialization (Python documentation)
B3-MLO-03-2.supports: Warning that the pickle module is not secure and malicious pickle data can execute arbitrary code during unpickling; only instance data is pickled, not class code; suggests signing data with hmac; protocol versions.

B3-MLO-03-2.title: Model persistence (scikit-learn user guide)
B3-MLO-03-2.supports: pickle/joblib are not safe for untrusted sources; loading across scikit-learn versions is unsupported and raises InconsistentVersionWarning; persisted models need the training environment; ONNX does not need a Python environment but not all estimators are supported and arbitrary computation can be represented (sandbox recommended).

B3-MLO-03-3.title: ONNX Intermediate Representation specification
B3-MLO-03-3.supports: ONNX specifies a portable serialized format of a computation graph; a model must name the operator sets it relies on and an implementation must support all operators in the set or reject the model; non-default operator sets must specify a domain.

B3-MLO-03-3.title: Model persistence (scikit-learn user guide)
B3-MLO-03-3.supports: pickle/joblib are not safe for untrusted sources; loading across scikit-learn versions is unsupported and raises InconsistentVersionWarning; persisted models need the training environment; ONNX does not need a Python environment but not all estimators are supported and arbitrary computation can be represented (sandbox recommended).

B3-MLO-03-3.title: sklearn-onnx: Issues when switching to float (float vs double)
B3-MLO-03-3.supports: Float/double comparisons in trees give the same result in most cases but can differ; ONNX ML only allows float coefficients for TreeEnsembleRegressor (regression example).

B3-MLO-03-4.title: MLflow Model Signatures
B3-MLO-03-4.supports: A signature specifies the expected format of inputs, outputs and parameters; it can be inferred automatically when an input_example is provided; helps deployment tools validate requests.

B3-MLO-03-4.title: MLflow source: _enforce_mlflow_datatype (mlflow/models/utils.py)
B3-MLO-03-4.supports: Lossy float->int conversion is rejected rather than truncated; error 'Can not safely convert'.

B3-MLO-03-4.title: MLflow source: type inference (mlflow/types/utils.py)
B3-MLO-03-4.supports: Integer-valued example data (Python int, np.int64) is inferred as an integer type (long), not double.

B3-MLO-03-5.title: MLflow Model Registry
B3-MLO-03-5.supports: Registry is a centralized model store with versioning (each registration increments the version), lineage to the producing run, tags and annotations; aliases are mutable named references to a model version.

B3-MLO-03-5.title: docker image pull: pull an image by digest
B3-MLO-03-5.supports: Pulling by digest specifies exactly which image version is used, supporting 'base image referenced by digest'.

B3-MLO-03-5.title: pip secure installs: hash-checking mode
B3-MLO-03-5.supports: A dependency lockfile with hashes lets pip verify downloaded packages.

B3-MLO-04-2.title: gRPC Deadlines
B3-MLO-04-2.supports: A deadline is a point in time past which a client is unwilling to wait; gRPC sets no deadline by default and the docs advise always setting a realistic one; deadlines can be propagated to downstream calls.

B3-MLO-04-2.title: gRPC Load Balancing (gRPC blog)
B3-MLO-04-2.supports: Proxy (L7) balancing can spread streams of one HTTP/2 connection across backends, which L3/L4 balancing does not; client-side balancing alternative.

B3-MLO-04-2.title: gRPC-Web basics (grpc.io)
B3-MLO-04-2.supports: gRPC-Web lets browsers access gRPC services; the guide's example uses an Envoy proxy to forward browser requests to the backend gRPC server (it does not itself state that native gRPC is impossible from browsers).

B3-MLO-04-4.title: Monitoring Distributed Systems (Google SRE Book)
B3-MLO-04-4.supports: Four golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation); distinguish latency of successful and failed requests; measure distributions/percentiles rather than only averages.

B3-MLO-04-5.title: Handling Overload (Google SRE Book)
B3-MLO-04-5.supports: Client-side retry budget of about 10% and per-request cap of three attempts.

B3-MLO-04-5.title: Addressing Cascading Failures (Google SRE Book)
B3-MLO-04-5.supports: Randomized exponential backoff, limit retries, load shedding, server skips work past the deadline, deadline propagation, retry-rate graphs as a diagnostic signal.

B3-MLO-04-6.supports: Four golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation); distinguish latency of successful and failed requests; measure distributions/percentiles rather than only averages.

B3-MLO-04-6.title: Alerting on SLOs (Google SRE Workbook)
B3-MLO-04-6.supports: Multiwindow, multi-burn-rate alerts for a 99.9% SLO: page at burn rate 14.4 (1 h long / 5 min short window) and 6 (6 h / 30 min); ticket at burn rate 1 (3 d / 6 h).

B3-MLO-04-6.title: GDPR Recital 26 (gdpr-info.eu reproduction)
B3-MLO-04-6.supports: Pseudonymised data that could be attributed to a person by additional information is still information on an identifiable person.

B3-MLO-04-7.title: Alerting on SLOs (Google SRE Workbook)
B3-MLO-04-7.supports: Burn rate is how fast the service consumes the error budget relative to the SLO; recommended multiwindow multi-burn-rate starting parameters (e.g. 14.4x burn over 1 hour and 5 minutes, 2% of budget consumed, for a 99.9% SLO).

B3-MLO-05-1.title: Canarying Releases (Google SRE Workbook)
B3-MLO-05-1.supports: Canarying is a partial, time-limited deployment of a change with evaluation, the rest of the service acting as control; canary should be large and long enough to be representative; a handful of queries gives no useful signal; response to a bad canary is to pause/roll back; keep the set of canary metrics small.

B3-MLO-05-1.title: BlueGreenDeployment (Martin Fowler)

B3-MLO-06-1.title: Docker Docs: Build cache
B3-MLO-06-1.supports: When a layer changes, all layers after it are rebuilt.

B3-MLO-06-1.title: Docker Docs: Optimize build cache
B3-MLO-06-1.supports: Put expensive, rarely changing steps early; copy package-management files first, install dependencies, then copy frequently changing source so dependency layers are not rebuilt.

B3-MLO-06-1.title: Docker Docs: Building best practices
B3-MLO-06-1.supports: Pinning a base image to a specific digest is supported for supply-chain integrity; use USER to run as non-root where privileges are not needed; .dockerignore excludes files from the build context.

B3-MLO-06-2.title: Kubernetes Docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
B3-MLO-06-2.supports: kube-scheduler places Pods using requests; memory limits are enforced by kernel OOM kills and CPU limits by throttling; OOMKilled means the container tried to use more memory than its limit; a Pod stays Pending while its request cannot be satisfied; extended resources must be whole numbers and cannot be overcommitted (request equals limit).

B3-MLO-06-2.title: Kubernetes Docs: Volumes (emptyDir)
B3-MLO-06-2.supports: emptyDir with medium Memory is a RAM-backed tmpfs, and files written to it count against the memory limit of the container that wrote them.

B3-MLO-06-3.title: Kubernetes Docs: Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
B3-MLO-06-3.supports: Liveness and readiness probes are not run until the startup probe succeeds; a failed startup probe makes the kubelet kill the container, subject to its restart policy; liveness probes do not wait for readiness; startup probes suit slow-starting containers.

B3-MLO-06-3.title: Kubernetes Docs: Configure Liveness, Readiness and Startup Probes
B3-MLO-06-3.supports: A pod whose containers report not ready receives no traffic through Services; a failed liveness check makes the kubelet kill and restart the container; readiness probes run during the container's whole lifecycle.

B3-MLO-06-4.title: Kubernetes Docs: Deployments
B3-MLO-06-4.supports: maxUnavailable and maxSurge definitions, both default to 25%, they cannot both be 0; minReadySeconds; old ReplicaSets are kept as revision history for rollback.

B3-MLO-06-4.title: Kubernetes Docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
B3-MLO-06-4.supports: kube-scheduler places Pods using requests; memory limits are enforced by kernel OOM kills and CPU limits by throttling; OOMKilled means the container tried to use more memory than its limit; a Pod stays Pending while its request cannot be satisfied; extended resources must be whole numbers and cannot be overcommitted (request equals limit).

B3-MLO-06-5.title: Kubernetes Docs: Schedule GPUs
B3-MLO-06-5.supports: GPUs are specified in limits; a limit alone is used as the request; if both are given they must be equal; node labels and node selectors can target nodes with particular GPU types.

B3-MLO-06-5.title: Kubernetes Docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
B3-MLO-06-5.supports: kube-scheduler places Pods using requests; memory limits are enforced by kernel OOM kills and CPU limits by throttling; OOMKilled means the container tried to use more memory than its limit; a Pod stays Pending while its request cannot be satisfied; extended resources must be whole numbers and cannot be overcommitted (request equals limit).

B3-MLO-06-5.title: Kubernetes Docs: Taints and Tolerations
B3-MLO-06-5.supports: Tainted nodes accept no new Pods without a matching toleration (NoSchedule), which can dedicate nodes to particular workloads.

B3-MLO-06-5.title: Kubernetes Docs: Gang Scheduling
B3-MLO-06-5.supports: Gang scheduling (all-or-nothing placement of a pod group) is now a feature-gated capability of the Kubernetes scheduler.

B3-MLO-06-5.title: Kubernetes Docs: Pod Priority and Preemption
B3-MLO-06-5.supports: Pod priority and preemption are core scheduler features and allow higher-priority pods to preempt lower-priority ones.

B3-MLO-06-6.title: Kubernetes Docs: Jobs
B3-MLO-06-6.supports: Jobs run tasks to completion with a backoffLimit for retries, and the same program may sometimes be started twice, so applications must handle being restarted.

B3-MLO-07-1.title: TensorFlow Data Validation guide
B3-MLO-07-1.supports: TFDV can detect distribution skew between training and serving data; drift is detected between consecutive spans; drift for categorical features is expressed as L-infinity distance.

B3-MLO-07-2.title: Feast Docs: Point-in-time joins
B3-MLO-07-2.supports: Feast joins features onto an entity dataframe in a point-in-time correct way, reproducing the state at each entity timestamp, and scans backward from that timestamp up to the TTL.

B3-MLO-07-2.title: Feast Docs: Feature view
B3-MLO-07-2.supports: A feature view's TTL limits how far back Feast looks when generating historical datasets; on-demand transformation logic is documented as executed in both historical and online retrieval paths.

B3-MLO-07-3.supports: Feast ingests feature values into an online store so that features can be served in real time with low latency.
